title: Explicit Matrices over $\mathbb Z_2$ with CNOT and Row Complexity $4n-\mathrm{o}(n)$ and Local Logic Gates
abstract: In this article, we present an explicit family of invertible $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb Z_2$ whose CNOT and row complexity is at least $4n-\text{o}(n)$; equivalently, reducing these matrices to the identity requires at least $4n-\text{o}(n)$ elementary row operations. Moreover, the same complexity lower bound holds in the stronger computational model where the CNOT gates are replaced by arbitrary local linear logic gates, namely arbitrary invertible linear transformations acting on pairs of coordinates.   Let $G_n$ denote the permutation group generated by local logic gates acting on the set of binary strings of length $n$. We prove that $G_n$ is naturally isomorphic to the group of all invertible affine transformations of the vector space $\mathbb Z_2^n$, thus reducing the problem of estimating the quantum complexity of permutations in $G_n$ to the row reduction complexity of invertible matrices over $\mathbb Z_2$. As an application, we show that the permutations associated with our explicit matrices have quantum complexity at least $4n-\text{o}(n)$.
summary: This paper develops a method to find explicit examples of matrices over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ that require a high number of elementary row operations ($4n - o(n)$) to reduce to identity. By showing that the complexity of local logic gates is equivalent to this matrix complexity, they establish a significant quantum complexity lower bound for these specific types of quantum circuits.
main_problem: The authors aim to establish a high lower bound on the quantum complexity required to implement permutations generated by local logic gates acting on $n$ qubits.
main_result: They construct an explicit family of matrices over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ whose CNOT and row-reduction complexity is at least $4n - o(n)$, establishing a corresponding lower bound for the quantum complexity of these permutations.
method: The problem is reduced to analyzing the row-reduction complexity of invertible matrices over $\mathbb{Z}_2$, utilizing techniques involving additive circuit complexity bounds derived from finite field theory and group isomorphism arguments.
model_or_system: The model involves qubits represented by binary strings of length $n$ ($\mathbb{Z}_2^n$). The operations are restricted to 'local logic gates,' which generate the group $	ext{AGL}(n, 2)$ (the group of invertible affine transformations on $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$).
key_observables: CNOT complexity ($\ell_n(A)$), row complexity ($\ell_{	ext{row}}(A)$), and quantum circuit complexity ($	ext{QC}(T)$).
important_parameters: $n$ (the number of qubits/length of the string); the lower bound $4n - o(n)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the permutation group generated by local logic gates is isomorphic to $	ext{AGL}(n, 2)$, allowing complexity estimation via matrix row reduction.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the equivalence between the quantum complexity of permutations in $G_n$ and the row-reduction complexity of their associated matrices. It then uses advanced algebraic techniques (related to additive circuit complexity) to construct explicit examples achieving the desired superlinear lower bound, culminating in a formal proof relating $	ext{QC}(T)$ to matrix complexity.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, high lower bounds on quantum computational resources needed for specific classes of gates (local logic gates), which is crucial for understanding the inherent difficulty of simulating certain physical processes or implementing universal quantum computation models.
